bruno-directed.source: Qwen3-TTS-1.7B VoiceDesign official hosted demo; see generation-requests.json and raw take metadata
bruno-directed.license: Apache-2.0 model; original fictional performance, no real-person recording or clone
bruno-directed.notes: A young adult male footballer with a bright, slightly raspy voice, SHOUTING furiously across a football pitch to get the referee's attention. Two explosive projected calls, the second louder and more outraged. Strong breath pressure, sharp attack and a stretched vowel. Comic theatrical indignation. This is a full-throated shout, not ordinary speech. Clean dry recording, no crowd.

oliver-directed.source: Qwen3-TTS-1.7B VoiceDesign official hosted demo; see generation-requests.json and raw take metadata
oliver-directed.license: Apache-2.0 model; original fictional performance, no real-person recording or clone
oliver-directed.notes: An adult British English man with a thin, pinched mid-high voice. He is tearfully begging for forgiveness, on the edge of a ridiculous emotional breakdown. His breath catches before the second so, his voice trembles and cracks on sorry into a pleading whimper. Play this as an embarrassed man trying and failing to hold back tears. Urgent and compressed, about two seconds. Clean dry close microphone, no music.

carrick-directed.source: Qwen3-TTS-1.7B VoiceDesign official hosted demo; see generation-requests.json and raw take metadata
carrick-directed.license: Apache-2.0 model; original fictional performance, no real-person recording or clone
carrick-directed.notes: A middle-aged British English man with a low, slightly gravelly voice and a restrained northern English accent. Bone-dry sarcasm, fed up but completely controlled. Deliver this short question as a cutting comeback, stress POINTS, then let with that fall dismissively. Brisk, about one and a half seconds, no introductory breath or extra words. A deadpan comic punchline. Clean dry close microphone, no music.
